svg.title: Q-learning on a cliff grid: the whole map
svg.desc: Six panels: the grid world, the Q table, the two readouts, one update, credit moving backward along the route, and the limits.

text.font-family: 'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive
text.tspan: Q-learning on a cliff grid: the whole map

text.font-family: 'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive
'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive

text.tspan: Blue dots: the best route, 13 steps
Stepping on a ✕ costs −100 and puts you back at S
Rows are counted from the top: S is cell (3, 0).

text.tspan: Q table: one row per cell, one column per move

text.tspan: Green: the largest number in the row
192 numbers in all. 44 belong to the cliff and the flag and stay 0.
Finished table, update 10,000. A move into the cliff holds about −112.

text.font-family: 'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive

text.tspan: Cell (2,1): one row gives two readouts

text.font-family: 'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive
text.tspan: the number in the grid cell

text.font-family: 'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive
text.tspan: the arrow in the grid cell
This cell agrees to two decimals: max Q ≈ max q* ≈ −10.47
Early tables are a guess: at update 2,000 the start cell read −9.73, optimum ≈ −12.25.

text.font-family: 'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive

text.tspan: Then s ← s′ and the loop repeats.
At the flag: target = r, nothing follows.
The −50 in the row of s′ is ignored: a larger number sits beside it.

text.font-family: 'Bradley Hand','Segoe Print','Chalkboard SE','Comic Neue','Comic Sans MS',cursive

g.desc: Recorded update 19 changes the right entry in cell (2,0) from zero to minus 0.5, lowering its row maximum to minus 0.5. Update 24 in neighboring cell (2,1) reads that maximum for a move left, producing target minus 1.495 and new value minus 0.7475. The smaller strip compares the calculated values at the optimum.
g.text: A good route can appear before its values settle.

svg.title: Expected Bellman maps shrink the worst table difference
